review.arm_order_and_temporal_bias_assessment: Update and heldout A/B order are deterministic SHA-based functions of stream/task/arm (ordered_arms with frozen salts), computed before outcomes. This is a reasonable way to avoid systematic A-first/B-second temporal bias without outcome-dependent randomization. No hidden order-selection path was found; the salts are constants and the ordering is recomputed identically on resume.
review.heldout_evaluation_assessment: Each state evaluates all the same 18 probes at K=1 with the same actor/verifier/model settings (temperature 0, thinking disabled, max_turns 10, max_output_tokens 4096, concurrency 1). Treating the 18 probes as repeated observations and the 12 stream pairs as independent units is correct. The execution code avoids scientific inference until the separate analysis step; the runner summary sets negative_control_inference_performed=False and the analysis script is a separate bound artifact.
review.identical_treatment_assessment: WIN-A and WIN-B are generated from the same initial SKILL.md (SHA-bound), the same exact eight pools per stream, and the same winner StreamProjection. The renderer computes WIN/MRW matched windows even though MRW is not executed; this is a legitimate prospective freeze for the later MRW comparison and does not compromise A/B identity because the same win_units list is passed to both arms and the evidence bundle SHA is frozen per stream before any arm executes. The V3.1 renderer is deterministic and arm-blinded, so both arms receive byte-identical pre-rendered winner evidence. The only intended difference is independent hosted provider calls and cloned persistent state.
review.mrw_separation_assessment: Zero MRW provider execution, zero RB-AGG, and zero method-effect inference in this full negative-control tranche. The runner sets mrw_executed=False, the evidence receipt sets mrw_provider_execution_authorized=False, and the analysis requires summary['mrw_executed'] is False. No MRW execution path exists; any such path would be P0.
nonblocking_notes: The renderer computes MRW matched windows prospectively; this is acceptable because it is a deterministic freeze for the later MRW comparison and does not affect WIN-A/WIN-B identity.
The planning expected provider calls (~2621) is below the structural maximum (4560); the structural maximum is the binding constraint and is not relaxed.
The bootstrap CI is a robustness check only and does not control the primary gate, which is correctly the paired TOST.
review.outcome_selection_and_failure_policy_ass: The nuisance gate was frozen before these outcomes. If equivalence fails, MRW is held because the causal contrast is not interpretable; this is not evidence against R17. This is legitimate and not an outcome-selective escape hatch because the failure policy is predeclared and the analysis script returns HOLD_UPDATER_OR_EVALUATOR_STOCHASTICITY with central_mechanism_adjudicated=False. If equivalence passes, it merely allows a separately contracted MRW experiment (prepare_mrw_contract=True, execute_mrw=False) rather than proving the mechanism.
